claim: An external reality exists independent of any observer's mind

evidence.title: Metaphysical Realism (SEP)
evidence.finding: Metaphysical realism holds that the world has a definite mind-independent structure

evidence.title: The Problem of Perception (SEP)
evidence.finding: The existence of an external world is a foundational assumption of nearly all epistemological frameworks

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Cannot be empirically verified from within experience — no measurement can prove the external world is not a simulation or dream
scoreReasoning.coherence: Consistent with all human experience and the entire scientific enterprise; denying it creates incoherence
scoreReasoning.convergence: Near-universal assumption across cultures, philosophies, and sciences; only challenged by edge-case philosophical positions
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Indispensable for any practical endeavor, science, technology, or daily life

claim: A proposition and its negation cannot both be true simultaneously in the same respect

evidence.title: Aristotle on Non-Contradiction (SEP)
evidence.finding: Aristotle held the LNC as the most certain of all principles, which cannot itself be demonstrated

evidence.title: Dialetheism (SEP)
evidence.finding: Dialetheists like Graham Priest argue some contradictions (dialetheia) are true, but this remains a minority position

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Not an empirical claim — it is a logical principle that cannot be tested by observation
scoreReasoning.coherence: Self-evident and foundational to classical logic, mathematics, and rational discourse
scoreReasoning.convergence: Accepted across virtually all logical traditions; dialetheism is a recognized but minority challenge
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All reasoning, computation, and technology depend on non-contradiction

claim: Human sensory perception, while fallible, systematically tracks features of external reality

evidence.title: Psychophysics: Weber-Fechner and Stevens' Laws
evidence.finding: Psychophysical laws demonstrate systematic, lawful relationships between physical stimuli and perceptual responses

evidence.title: Epistemological Problems of Perception (SEP)
evidence.finding: Despite illusions and biases, perception reliably tracks environmental features as evidenced by successful organism-environment interaction

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Psychophysics provides direct measurements showing perception tracks physical quantities, though with known biases and illusions
scoreReasoning.coherence: Consistent with evolutionary theory (perception evolved for fitness) and cognitive science
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad agreement across psychophysics, neuroscience, and evolutionary biology; philosophical debate remains about veridicality
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All empirical science and daily survival depend on perception being broadly reliable

claim: Observed regularities in nature can be extrapolated to unobserved cases with justified (though defeasible) confidence

evidence.title: The Problem of Induction (SEP)
evidence.finding: Hume showed induction cannot be justified by deduction or by induction itself, yet it remains indispensable to all empirical reasoning

evidence.title: Bayesian Epistemology (SEP)
evidence.finding: Bayesian frameworks provide a probabilistic justification for inductive inference, though foundational questions remain

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Hume's problem of induction remains formally unsolved — no empirical test can prove that nature will continue to be uniform
scoreReasoning.coherence: Deeply embedded in all scientific and everyday reasoning despite lacking deductive justification
scoreReasoning.convergence: Philosophers broadly agree induction is justified pragmatically; formal justification remains debated
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: All of science, technology, and practical decision-making depends on inductive reasoning

claim: Valid deductive arguments preserve truth from premises to conclusions

evidence.title: Logical Consequence (SEP)
evidence.finding: Deductive validity guarantees truth-preservation: if premises are true, the conclusion must be true in every model

evidence.title: Proof Theory (SEP)
evidence.finding: Formal proof systems demonstrate that valid deduction preserves truth through syntactic transformation rules

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Validity is a formal/logical property, not an empirical one — it cannot be measured by experiment
scoreReasoning.coherence: Central to all mathematical and logical reasoning; soundness and completeness theorems support this
scoreReasoning.convergence: Near-universal agreement across logical traditions; non-classical logics modify but don't reject validity
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Mathematics, computer science, and formal reasoning all depend on deductive validity

claim: Knowledge can be characterized as justified, true belief, subject to Gettier-type refinements

evidence.title: The Analysis of Knowledge (SEP)
evidence.finding: JTB was the standard analysis of knowledge until Gettier (1963) showed counterexamples; refined versions (defeasibility, reliabilism) continue the tradition

evidence.title: Is Justified True Belief Knowledge? (Gettier 1963)
evidence.finding: Gettier cases show JTB is necessary but not sufficient for knowledge; additional conditions needed

scoreReasoning.correspondence: Not empirically testable — this is a conceptual analysis of what knowledge means
scoreReasoning.coherence: Well-integrated into epistemology, though the Gettier problem shows it needs refinement
scoreReasoning.convergence: JTB as a starting point is widely accepted; disagreement on what additional conditions are needed
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: Provides a workable framework for distinguishing knowledge from mere opinion in practice

claim: Human knowledge acquisition through logic, perception, and induction is reliable enough to produce justified true beliefs about an external reality

evidence.title: Epistemology (SEP)
evidence.finding: Contemporary epistemology broadly affirms that human cognitive faculties, while fallible, produce knowledge when properly exercised

evidence.title: Reliabilism (SEP)
evidence.finding: Reliabilist theories hold that knowledge is produced by cognitive processes that are in fact reliable, even if we cannot prove this a priori

scoreReasoning.correspondence: The meta-claim that knowledge acquisition works cannot be directly measured — it is assessed by its fruits
scoreReasoning.coherence: Integrates all lower-level epistemic claims into a coherent picture of human cognitive capability
scoreReasoning.convergence: Broad philosophical and scientific consensus that human cognition is reliable enough for knowledge, with acknowledged limitations
scoreReasoning.pragmatism: The entire scientific and technological enterprise is evidence that human knowledge acquisition works
